4c2724d076.q: What approach should leaders take when employees don't get promoted internally?
4c2724d076.a: Leaders must be prepared to explain why someone didn't get a promotion and have forethought about what they will tell the unsuccessful candidates. If you don't have a set policy on how people get promoted within an organization, it can cause significant harm. Organizations should sit down with the people who didn't get the job and explain the reasons, helping them understand the pathways they need to pursue, so they don't leave the organization or become disengaged.
4c2724d076.e: Ep#263 Losing not getting the Thing
4c2724d076.rq: Most people want to know what the pathways are, what they need. And if they can't get there, then you better be honest with them because you're hanging them around with a false hope.

059037883a.q: How can leaders build psychological safety when projects or initiatives fail?
059037883a.a: The best leaders conduct a debrief or postmortem to find out what can be learned from the failure. If leaders blow up when things fail, everybody goes underground—no one volunteers and no one takes risks because they fear their heads will be chopped off. In fear-oriented organizations, people don't even tell you they're losing, and by the time you find out, it's too late.

2dab312632.q: What should hiring managers do after rejecting candidates in job interviews?
2dab312632.a: Hiring managers should proactively reach out to rejected candidates and offer to discuss the decision. When feedback is provided—such as explaining that the hired candidate had more experience or that a required course was missing—it allows the candidate to understand what they need to develop. This shows care and helps build relationships even after rejection.

4f59e5e63c.q: How do great leaders develop career resilience instead of rigid career paths?
4f59e5e63c.a: Instead of promising a clear career path, leaders can commit to evolving employees' skills so they have multiple pathways for growth. This means strengthening strategic thinking, critical thinking, and data management capabilities. When leaders are honest and say there are multiple career paths but commit to developing the right skills, people get excited and feel supported.

46c464eb4b.q: Why do managers sometimes ghost candidates after multiple interviews?
46c464eb4b.a: When candidates go through multiple interviews and several weeks later receive a generic rejection email without feedback, it damages the organization's brand internally and externally. People talk about this widely—if a company took six hours of your time through interviews and then ghosted you, that spreads. It's demoralizing for internal candidates and hurts an organization's reputation externally.
